title: Coordinate projection of a three-point indicator
statement: Let $J\subseteq\{0,1\}$ and let $x:\{0,1\}\to\{a,b,c\}$. Under the product of the uniform distributions on $\{a,b,c\}$, average the indicator that both coordinates equal $c$, while keeping the coordinates in $J$ fixed at $x$. The resulting value is $\prod_{i=0}^{1}\bigl(\mathbf{1}_{i\in J}\mathbf{1}_{x(i)=c}+(1-\mathbf{1}_{i\in J})/3\bigr)$, where each indicator is $1$ when its condition holds and $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: J is a subset of the two coordinate indices
x assigns one of the three points to each coordinate
